synthcheck

Experimental. synthcheck checks how authentic synthetic survey respondents are: Whether respondents generated by large language models resemble the real people they are meant to stand in for.

It looks at three things:

  • Overlap: Do synthetic respondents land where real people land?
  • Structure: Do the items relate to each other as they do in real people?
  • Behaviour: Do synthetic respondents answer the way people do, including variability, extreme and midpoint answers, acquiescence, consistency and person fit?

Each index is anchored between a shuffled baseline (0) and a second sample of real people (100). The synthetic authenticity benchmark compares several models in one table, scored by their weakest column by default.

Three diagnostics sit beside the benchmark and do not change its score: synthetic_construct() checks whether the scales hold together and relate as they do in real people (trait correlations, alpha and Tucker’s congruence against a permutation null), respondent_coverage() checks whether every real person has a synthetic look-alike, and authenticity_benchmark(copula = TRUE) adds a Gaussian copula row, a generator without a language model, as a reference.

The package compares models and supports decisions about them. It does not show that synthetic respondents can replace a field test.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("okanbulut/synthcheck")

Example 

library(synthcheck)

# Honesty-Humility, Canada: real people and six language models
h <- hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$trait == "H"]
rev_items <- intersect(h, hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$reverse])
keyed <- function(d) { d <- d[h]; d[rev_items] <- 8 - d[rev_items]; d }

real <- keyed(hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ])
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada" & hexaco_llm$attempt <= 4, ]
synthetic <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model, drop = TRUE),
                    function(m) lapply(split(m, m$attempt), keyed))

cov <- synthetic_coverage(synthetic, real, cor = "pearson")
cov
gg_coverage(cov)

The synthetic authenticity benchmark takes the raw answers and the item table, and does the keying itself:

real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada", ]
synthetic <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model), function(m) split(m, m$attempt))

bm <- authenticity_benchmark(synthetic, real, hexaco_items)
bm
gg_benchmark(bm)

# the eight behaviour features behind the Behaviour column
gg_behaviour(bm$behaviour)

# with a Gaussian copula row as a reference
bm <- authenticity_benchmark(synthetic, real, hexaco_items, copula = TRUE)

# diagnostics
gg_construct(synthetic_construct(synthetic, real, hexaco_items))
gg_respondent_coverage(respondent_coverage(synthetic, real, hexaco_items))

Generating synthetic data in an app

run_synthcheck_app() opens an app that does the whole workflow: Define an instrument and personas, generate synthetic respondents with Anthropic, OpenAI or local Ollama models (with their temperature and the number of attempts), watch a progress bar with the time left, save the data as CSV, JSON, RDS or Excel, and benchmark the models against real data with a plain-language summary for each one.

install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "ellmer", "callr", "jsonlite"))
res <- run_synthcheck_app(real = my_real_data)
res$benchmark

API keys typed into the app stay in memory for that session only. Keys set as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY in .Renviron are used without being shown. The same steps work in code:

ins <- sc_instrument(hexaco_items[hexaco_items$trait == "H", ], scale = c(1, 7))
per <- sc_persona_grid(age = c(25, 45, 65), country = c("Canada", "the United States"),
                       template = "You are a {age}-year-old adult living in {country}.")
syn <- generate_synthetic(ins, list(sc_model("anthropic"), sc_model("openai")), per,
                          attempts = 5, respondents = 10, parallel = 8, output = "my_run")

real <- hexaco_real[hexaco_real$country == "Canada", ]
bm <- authenticity_benchmark(as_synthetic_list(syn), real, ins$items)
summarise_benchmark(bm)

See the website for a Get started article, tutorials on each step and a tour of the app with demos.

Data

hexaco_real holds 17,874 real respondents to the 240 IPIP-HEXACO items from Canada, Great Britain and the United States (Open-Source Psychometrics Project). hexaco_llm holds 89,597 synthetic respondents from six language models (10 attempts per country), and hexaco_items holds the item text, facets and keys.
